page: Microsoft Azure M208s_v2 is a memory-optimized server belonging to the MSv2 family. It is powered by dedicated Intel Xeon 8280L processors with an x86_64 architecture, featuring 104 physical cores and 208 vCPUs running at 2.7 GHz. The system is equipped with 2850.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 13.7 GB of RAM per core. Local storage consists of a 4194 GB SSD, and the instance is Premium Storage capable. Virtualization is managed via Microsoft Hyper-V.

Benchmark data reveals a clear tradeoff between single-core and multi-core performance. Single-core metrics, such as stress-ng single-core CPU performance and Geekbench single-core scores, fall into the bottom 25% tier. Conversely, multi-core capabilities are highly competitive, with stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression ranking in the top 10%. Memory bandwidth is exceptionally high, with cached read-only small block bandwidth reaching 10456.14 GB/sec and uncached large block write bandwidth at 191.08 GB/sec, both placing in the top 10%. Redis SET operations also perform in the top tier, executing 153.96 million operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the M208s_v2 represents a high-density resource profile designed for massive memory footprints rather than raw single-threaded speed. The high ratio of RAM to vCPUs makes it highly suitable for memory-intensive enterprise workloads. Recommended use cases include large-scale relational databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, enterprise resource planning systems, and heavy multi-threaded data processing tasks that can leverage the massive parallel execution capabilities of its 208 vCPUs.
